composite_primary_keys.rationale: The grammar's only key-related production is a per-attribute, comma-separated list of key tokens (PK, FK, UK) attached to a single attribute row. There is no production that groups two or more attribute rows into one composite-key structure; the AST built from this grammar has no 'composite key' node at all. Marking two rows both PK produces two independent key flags in the data model, not a composite-key semantic — confirmed independently by open issue #3582 in source-mermaid-erd-contrary-evidence.json, which asks how to even notate a composite-key member.

self_referencing_foreign_keys_multiple.citation: erDb.ts, addRelationship() — entA and entB are accepted as independent strings with no equality check between them; addEntity() is idempotent (checks this.entities.has(name) before creating), so repeated self-references to the same entity do not conflict
self_referencing_foreign_keys_multiple.rationale: Nothing in the relationship-registration code path rejects entA === entB, and nothing limits how many relSpec statements may name the same entity pair. Three FK attribute rows plus three self-referencing relationship statements with distinct labels are all independently legal under this code.

several_logical_schemas_in_one_database.citation: erDiagram.jison — no NAMESPACE, SCHEMA, or subgraph-equivalent token or production exists in the ER grammar (contrast with the classDiagram grammar, which defines a separate namespace construct not shared with erDiagram)
several_logical_schemas_in_one_database.rationale: The ER grammar's only structural containers are 'entity' (with its attribute list) and 'relationship'; there is no grouping production. A schema/namespace concept would have to be bolted on outside the language (e.g. naming convention or a post-processing script), which is not an in-DSL workaround.

cross_cutting_validator_convention.citation: erDb.ts — addEntity/addRelationship perform structural bookkeeping (assigning ids, registering attributes) with no rule-evaluation or assertion logic anywhere in the module
cross_cutting_validator_convention.rationale: The database module that backs the parser is purely a structure-builder for rendering; it contains no concept of a declarative rule, lint check, or cross-entity assertion. Any such convention check would have to be implemented entirely outside Mermaid, against the raw .mmd text or the rendered output.

malformed_or_semantically_inconsistent_d.citation: erDb.ts, addRelationship() and addEntity() — a relationship statement naming an entity with no prior attribute-block declaration silently calls addEntity(entA), which creates a new empty EntityNode rather than raising an error
malformed_or_semantically_inconsistent_d.rationale: This is the single most load-bearing finding for the incumbent-replacement question: a relationship line that references an undeclared entity (the textbook example of a semantically inconsistent ERD — e.g. a typo'd entity name) is NOT rejected. It is silently auto-vivified into a new, attribute-less entity and rendered as if it were intentional. Mermaid's ER parser therefore has no semantic-consistency check of this kind at all; only lexical/grammatical syntax errors (e.g. an unterminated string, a malformed cardinality token) would fail parsing. See source-mermaid-erd-tooling.json for how this interacts with mmdc's exit-code behaviour.

contrary_evidence_search.result: No grammar production or database-layer check was found that groups attributes into composite keys, defines schema/namespace containers for erDiagram, or rejects a relationship statement naming a previously-undeclared entity. The absence of a throw/error path in addEntity/addRelationship on the undeclared-entity case was the specific, actively-searched-for negative result this record set out to establish.
